info.name: DPAY v1 — Merchant API
info.description:
The DPAY merchant API (v1), as executed.

Every example response in this collection was produced by sending that exact request to the DPAY API and recording the answer — status, headers and body — with the payment gateways' wire legs simulated. Nothing here is hand-written; the collection is regenerated from the API and a build fails if it drifts.

**Variables.** Requests use `{{base_url}}` and `Authorization: Bearer {{api_token}}`. Select the *Sandbox* environment (a sandbox token, `sb_tk_…`, from the dashboard) to rehearse against `/api/sandbox/*`, or the *Live* environment (an integration token from Settings → API Tokens) for the live endpoints. `{{session_id}}` is the session you are working with; `{{webhook_secret}}` is your endpoint's `whsec_` secret for verifying webhook signatures.

**Placeholders in examples.** Values that change on every call — timestamps, gateway references, the receipt token, request ids, signatures — appear as Postman variables (for example `{{expired_at}}`) in the example bodies and headers. Each has a sample value in this collection's variables, in the exact wire format, so you can see what to expect. Row ids (`session_id`, `payment_id`) are real and stable.

**Conventions.** JSON in, JSON out, always (the API ignores your Accept header). Amounts are LYD major units with up to three decimals (Mastercard: USD). Slashes inside JSON strings are escaped as `\/`. Errors: 422 `{message, errors}` for validation; `{message, status}` for 401 (unauthenticated) and 429 (throttled); `{message}` for 403 and 400 business refusals (not authorized, not found, not pending, unsupported…); the token-ability 403 adds `error` and `required_abilities`. Answers are `content-type: application/json`, except those the framework's exception layer writes — the 401 and 429 `{message, status}` bodies, the token-ability 403 and the field-validation 422s — which add `; charset=utf-8`: match the media type, not the whole header (the examples show which is which). The general limit is 60 requests per minute per token (verify: 5, open: 20).

**Examples.** Each request carries its executed examples. An example's *original request* is the request that produced it: where it differs from the request above it (a bogus bearer for a 401, an unknown id for a 404, the session a read really read), the difference is spelled out.

item.name: Payment sessions
item.description: The core flow: open a session for a gateway, hand the customer the OTP prompt or the payment link, verify, receive the webhook. Amounts are LYD major units with up to three decimals; the platform fee is added on top (`total`) and the session is stored at the charged amount.

item.name: Open a session
item.description: POST /api/payment/sessions/open — one request per gateway. `pay_method` selects the gateway and decides which extra fields are required. Sessions expire: Moamalat and Sadad after 10 minutes, Mastercard after 30, every other gateway after 15. The idempotent variant shows what a replayed `Idempotency-Key` returns.

request.description: No gateway-specific fields. The response carries `payment_link`: send the customer there to pay by card in the Moamalat LightBox. Expires in 10 minutes. `amount` echoes the request; `total` is what the customer is charged.

item.name: Verify
item.description: POST /api/payment/sessions/verify — the customer's OTP for the OTP gateways (EDFali, Sadad, MobiCash, the MITF banks), or the LightBox callback for Moamalat. Moamalat verification is PUBLIC (the LightBox posts it from the customer's browser); every other gateway requires the session owner's bearer. Throttled at 5 requests per minute per caller.

request.description: The 4-digit OTP the customer received. On success the session is `paid`, a payment row is booked (`payment`), the webhook fires and `receipt_url` is the customer's receipt. The flat trailing fields repeat the nested payment — both are the contract. A second call on a paid session answers "already verified".

item.name: Verify — EDFali wrong OTP, then lock-out

request.description: A rejected OTP leaves the session pending and the customer may retry; the bank's reason is the message. The 5th failed attempt locks the session (`failed`, `payment.failed` webhook) and answers the lock-out message; from then on the session is not pending. Sadad shares the 5-attempt budget; MobiCash and the MITF banks have no counter.

item.name: Sandbox
item.description: The same endpoints under /api/sandbox, authenticated with a sandbox token (`sb_tk_…`, issued from the dashboard) and never touching a real gateway. Magic OTPs: `111111` pays, `000000` is a final decline, anything else is a retryable invalid OTP. Differences from live are deliberate and documented on each request: fee rounded to 2 dp with an unrounded total, no `currency` key, `sandbox: true`, decimal-string amounts on reads, a flat 5-minute expiry that is applied lazily on read, and Sadad / Mastercard unsupported. Since A34 the sandbox open honours `Idempotency-Key` exactly as live does (≤ 64 characters — longer is a 422, never truncated), so a plugin's test mode exercises the live code path; the idempotent request below shows the first open and its replay.

request.description: Same request as live. Differences in the answer: `fee_amount` is rounded to 2 dp and `total` is the unrounded sum, there is no `currency`, `sandbox: true` is added, and the session lives 5 minutes. `customer_mobile` is only checked for presence here.

item.name: Checkout Sessions
item.description: The hosted checkout (amendment A34): create a checkout session for a DECIMAL LYD amount (up to 2 dp), send the customer to its `url` — a DPAY-branded, Arabic-first page listing every method you have enabled — and let DPAY collect. Your integration never sees a mobile number, a bank card identifier or an OTP. Four steps: create → redirect → on return, RE-READ the session (`GET …/{id}`; the return query is a hint, never the truth) → consume the `checkout.*` webhooks and reconcile pending orders every few minutes. `/api/v2` conventions: `{data, meta}` envelopes, RFC 7807 problems (`application/problem+json`), ISO-8601 timestamps with milliseconds, decimal-string amounts. The same paths accept a sandbox token (`sb_tk_…`): ids mint as `cs_test_…`, the page is `/sandbox/pay/{id}`, the magic OTPs apply, and `live` is false. Status machine: `open → paid | expired | cancelled`, and `expired → paid` when a bank confirms an attempt after the checkout expired (the money is taken; `checkout.completed` then follows `checkout.expired`) — `expired` is NOT final, accept `paid` from any prior state. A mobile-app session token (`mobile_auth_token`) is refused on these paths (403 `mobile_token_not_allowed`).

request.description:
A merchant-priced intent for a decimal LYD `amount` (≤ 2 dp — a third decimal is a 422 on `errors.amount`; it is your figure BEFORE the per-method fee). `reference` is your order number; `return_url` (https) is where the customer lands afterwards, `cancel_url` where "return to store" goes (defaults to `return_url`); `metadata` (≤ 50 scalar keys) comes back on every read and webhook; `customer` pre-fills the page. Answers **201** with the session: `url` is the hosted page — redirect the customer there. `status` is `open` for `expires_in_minutes` (default 60, 5…1440). Requires `payments.create`.

Always send `Idempotency-Key` (≤ 64 chars; key it on your order and attempt, e.g. `{platform}:{store}:{order}:{attempt}`): a retried request returns the ORIGINAL session — same `id`, same `url` — with **200** and `meta.idempotent_replay: true` instead of creating a second one. The key is scoped to your account and the environment and bound to the session for its whole life; never reuse one for a different order. Works in the sandbox too.

item.name: Webhooks (outbound)
item.description: Requests DPAY sends to YOUR endpoint — documented here, not runnable against DPAY. Every terminal transition of a session (`payment.paid`, `payment.failed`, `payment.expired`, `payment.refunded`, `payment.voided`) posts the payload below to each active endpoint subscribed to the event, signed with the endpoint's `whsec_` secret: `X-DPAY-Signature = HMAC-SHA256('{X-DPAY-Timestamp}.{raw body}', secret)`, lowercase hex. Verify over the exact bytes you received (the body is PHP-style JSON: `/` is escaped as `\/`), reject timestamps older than 5 minutes, answer any 2xx within 15 seconds, and de-duplicate on `session_id` + `event` (`checkout_session_id` + `event` for the checkout events) — deliveries retry up to 5 times (1 min, 5 min, 15 min, 1 hour). `live` is false for sandbox sessions.

request.description:
Sent when a live session is settled — here the EDFali session verified above. `amount` is the charged amount; `data` is the stored session data; `system_reference` / `network_reference` / `paid_through` / `payer_account` are null for gateways that do not report them.

This request is what DPAY sends to your endpoint; it is not runnable against the API. The body is the exact bytes signed by X-DPAY-Signature.

The same event for a sandbox session — here the Moamalat session settled above with `moamalat_response`. `live` is false; `system_reference` is the callback's `SystemReference`. Whether an endpoint receives it is its mode in the dashboard: live, sandbox or both.

This request is what DPAY sends to your endpoint; it is not runnable against the API. The body is the exact bytes signed by X-DPAY-Signature.

Sent when a session is declined — here the sandbox session declined with OTP 000000. `live` is false. `paid_at` still names the session `updated_at`.

This request is what DPAY sends to your endpoint; it is not runnable against the API. The body is the exact bytes signed by X-DPAY-Signature.

Sent ONCE when a pending session is found past its expiry — on verify, on read, or by the sweeper. Here the sandbox session read after its 5-minute window.

This request is what DPAY sends to your endpoint; it is not runnable against the API. The body is the exact bytes signed by X-DPAY-Signature.

The unchanged `payment.paid` for an ATTEMPT of a hosted checkout — here the EDFali attempt that paid the checkout session above. `data` carries `checkout_session_id`, `reference`, `description` and `metadata` from the checkout, next to the per-attempt `original_amount` / `fee_percent` / `fee_amount`. If you already handle `payment.*`, this is how an attempt names its checkout.

This request is what DPAY sends to your endpoint; it is not runnable against the API. The body is the exact bytes signed by X-DPAY-Signature.

Sent ONCE when a hosted checkout is paid — inside the same database transaction as the winning attempt's `payment.paid`, so the two are delivered together or not at all. `amount` is your figure before the fee; `payment.amount_charged` the 2 dp fee-inclusive charge; `created_at` is the checkout's creation, `occurred_at` the settlement. De-duplicate on `checkout_session_id` + `event`; verify the signature over the raw bytes; then mark the order paid.

This request is what DPAY sends to your endpoint; it is not runnable against the API. The body is the exact bytes signed by X-DPAY-Signature.

Sent ONCE when an open checkout passes `expires_at` — on a read (the hosted page, the status endpoint) or by the sweeper. `payment` is null. Treat it as "free the order for another attempt", not as an automatic cancellation: your pending-order policy decides.

This request is what DPAY sends to your endpoint; it is not runnable against the API. The body is the exact bytes signed by X-DPAY-Signature.

Sent ONCE when you cancel a checkout through the API. `payment` is null. A customer leaving the hosted page never produces this event — the session stays open until it expires.

This request is what DPAY sends to your endpoint; it is not runnable against the API. The body is the exact bytes signed by X-DPAY-Signature.

The same event for a sandbox checkout — here the one paid above with the magic OTP `111111`. `live` is false and `payment.receipt_url` is null. An endpoint receives it according to its mode in the dashboard (live, sandbox or both); refuse a `live: false` event while your integration is in live mode.

This request is what DPAY sends to your endpoint; it is not runnable against the API. The body is the exact bytes signed by X-DPAY-Signature.

variable.description: Session expiry — bare Carbon serialisation: ISO-8601 with six fractional digits and a literal Z. Set by the API from the gateway expiry table (Moamalat/Sadad 10 min, Mastercard 30, others 15; sandbox flat 5).
Creation time in the toIso8601String() form (offset, no microseconds) — the nested payment object and the webhook payload.
Webhook payload: the session `updated_at` in the toIso8601String() form — named paid_at for every event, including failed and expired.
Paginated Payment rows: created_at in the bare Carbon form (microseconds + Z).
Paginated Payment rows: updated_at in the bare Carbon form (microseconds + Z).
GET /api/health: the server time in the toIso8601String() form.
Live gateway reference: `txn_` + 32 hex chars (random_bytes(16)). Sadad overwrites it with the bank transaction id; Mastercard with the receipt after capture.
Sandbox gateway reference: `sb_txn_` + 32 hex chars.
Receipt URL token: the first 32 hex chars of HMAC-SHA256(`{session_id}|{created_at unix}`, APP_KEY). Opaque to merchants.
Sandbox Moamalat pay-page token in payment_link: first 32 hex chars of HMAC-SHA256(`sandbox|{session_id}|{created_at unix}`, APP_KEY).
x-request-id response header: a UUID minted per request (or echoed from the inbound header). Quote it in support tickets.
429 only: seconds until the throttle window resets (Retry-After).
429 only: unix time at which the throttle window resets (x-ratelimit-reset).
Moamalat LightBox callback TxnDate: yyMMddHHmmss in Africa/Tripoli local time. The API rejects callbacks more than 30 minutes away from its own clock.
Moamalat LightBox callback Amount: the charged total in DIRHAM (LYD × 1000) — the one place the wire is not major units. 256250 is 256.250 LYD.
Moamalat LightBox callback SecureHash: uppercase hex HMAC-SHA256 computed by the LightBox with the merchant secure key. Your integration forwards it verbatim; it is never built client-side.

A live checkout session id (A34): `cs_` + a 26-char Crockford ULID with 80 random bits — the hosted URL's only secret. Set it from a Create response; an environment variable of the same name overrides this sample.
A sandbox checkout session id: `cs_test_` + a 26-char Crockford ULID.
Checkout session `expires_at` — `created_at` + `expires_in_minutes` (default 60), in the v2 form: ISO-8601 with milliseconds and a literal Z.
v2 `created_at` (checkout sessions, their attempts): ISO-8601 with milliseconds and a literal Z.
v2 `updated_at`: ISO-8601 with milliseconds and a literal Z.
v2 `paid_at` — when the winning attempt settled (checkout session and its `payment` block).
v2 `cancelled_at` — when the merchant cancelled the checkout session.
checkout.* webhook: when the transition happened (paid, expired, cancelled), toIso8601String() form. `created_at` beside it is the checkout's creation time.
Outbound webhook X-DPAY-Timestamp: unix seconds at send time.
Outbound webhook X-DPAY-Signature: lowercase hex HMAC-SHA256(`{X-DPAY-Timestamp}.{raw body}`, webhook_secret). Verify over the raw bytes you received.
Your HTTPS endpoint as configured in the dashboard. DPay only delivers to https:// URLs that resolve to a public address.
An integration token belonging to a DIFFERENT merchant — only used to show the cross-tenant refusals. You cannot obtain one; the example is here so the 403 body is documented.
A bearer that authenticates but carries neither the role:api nor the role:session ability — only used to show the insufficient_token_ability 403.
